The Purdue Beta Mu chapter site identifies its chapter house at 150 Littleton Street, and Purdue BoilerLink lists the same address for Beta Theta Pi.
identity_crosswalk.master_asset_match: No reliable pre-existing asset match was present in the project library; this new asset explicitly represents GIS FID 826.

asset.coordinate_frame: Meters, X east, Y north, Z up; campus project origin latitude 40.4274, longitude -86.9137.
asset.geometry_summary: Exact GIS perimeter walls with the repeated closing vertex removed; a continuous closed slate roof shell tessellated within the concave GIS footprint, with a shallow photo-derived north-south ridge; three facade levels, a pale projecting bay with three stacked arched glazed openings, two west-wing gabled dormers, and an arched stone entrance with a raised Beta Mu shield and brass chevron.
asset.materials: Portable node materials: procedural warm red-brown brick, charcoal slate, limestone trim, cream-painted window frames, dark reflective glass, and aged-brass entrance crest details. No external material paths or unpacked image dependencies.
asset.interior: Not modeled. Purdue GIS references a private G: drive floorplan path, but no registered public plan was available. The official Beta housing record says four floors and a basement; it does not establish which levels are above grade or supply an interior plan, so interior geometry remains omitted.

measurements.method: Transform the EPSG:4326 ring to project campus XY using X=(longitude + 86.9137)*111412.84*cos(radians(40.4274)); Y=(latitude - 40.4274)*111040.0; compute polygon area, perimeter, and axis-aligned bounds in those local approximate meters.
measurements.area_note: The GIS Shape__Area value is in web-Mercator units, whose scale inflates ground area at this latitude. The local approximate area above is derived from the returned polygon ring, not copied from Shape__Area.

sources.uncertainty: The GIS footprint is authoritative for plan placement. The local coordinate transform is approximate, not a surveyed CRS. GIS NUM_LEVELS=1 conflicts with the three visible facade levels in official photos, while Extrution=12 has no interpretable units in the available metadata; neither provides a reliable height.

modelling_decisions.footprint: Used the full official FID 826 polygon ring after the documented campus-coordinate transform; wall perimeter and roof eaves follow this GIS geometry.
modelling_decisions.height: Wall height is modeled at approximately 9.3 m to represent three visible above-grade facade levels. The official Beta housing page lists four floors and a basement, but does not clarify whether the reported floor count includes the basement; this model choice is therefore photographic, not surveyed. Purdue GIS NUM_LEVELS=1 and Extrution=12 remain conflicting/unclear fields.
modelling_decisions.roof: Rebuilt the roof as one continuous watertight shell. The top surface is tessellated inside the exact concave GIS footprint and shares every perimeter vertex with the eave walls; its shallow north-south height field is a photo-derived pitch estimate. Two small west-facing gabled dormers are modeled on the slate wings from the official chapter-house elevations. Boundary edges, nonmanifold edges, and zero-area roof faces audit to zero; all 17 top facets point upward. This avoids the prior open, mismatched Y-band facets and self-crossing cap. Roof form remains an approximation because no surveyed ridge/elevation measurements or geo-registered orthogonal photos were available.
modelling_decisions.windows_and_entrance: Three visible facade levels use repeating divided sash windows; east/rear openings are modeled on the opposite elevation. The pale projecting bay has three stacked arched glazed openings. The entry has a segmented stone arch, dark wood door, transom, steps, pale plaque, raised red shield, and brass chevron detail. Facade bearing and exact opening coordinates remain approximate because imagery does not geo-register the photographed elevation to a GIS edge.
modelling_decisions.interior: Omitted because no registered floor plan was available to substantiate its geometry.
